sp.p: You'll have an excellent father-in-law. Sir John positively weeps when he talks of your income!

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Sir John, possibly—but Georgina?

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: Plays affection to you in the afternoon, after practising first with Sir Frederick in the morning.

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: On your life, Sir, be serious: what do you mean?

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: That in passing this way I see her very often walking in the square with Sir Frederick.

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Ha! say you so?

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: What then? Man is born to be deceived. You look nervous—your hand trembles; that comes of gaming. They say at the clubs that you play deeply.

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Ha! ha! Do they say that?—a few hundreds lost or won—a cheap opiate—anything that can lay the memory to sleep. The poor man drinks and the rich man gambles—the same motive to both! But you are right—it is a base resource—I will play no more.

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: I am delighted to hear it, for your friend Captain Smooth has ruined half the young heirs in London. To play with him is to advertise yourself a bankrupt. Even Sir John is alarmed. I met him just now in Pall Mall; he made me stop, and implored me to speak to you. By the by, I forgot—do you bank with Flash, Brisk, Credit, and Co.?

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: So, Sir John is alarmed?—
Gulled by this cogging charlatan?—Aha! I may beat him yet at his own weapons!—Humph! Bank with Flash! Why do you ask me?

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: Because Sir John has just heard that they are in a very bad way, and begs you to withdraw anything you have in their hands.

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: I'll see to it. So Sir John is alarmed at my gambling?

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: Terribly! He even told me he should go himself to the club, this evening, to watch you.

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: To watch me!—good—I will be there.

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: But you will promise not to play.

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Yes—to play. I feel it is impossible to give it up!

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: No—no! 'Sdeath, man! be as wretched as you please: break your heart, that's nothing! but damme, take care of your pockets!

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: I will be there—I will play with Captain Smooth— I will lose as much as I please—thousands—millions— billions; and if he presume to spy on my losses, hang me if I don't lose Sir John himself into the bargain!

I am so absent! What was the bank you mentioned? Flash, Brisk, and Credit. Bless me, how unlucky! and it's too late to draw out to-day. Tell Sir John I'm very much obliged to him, and he'll find me at the club any time before daybreak hard at work with my friend Smooth!

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: He's certainly crazy! but I don't wonder at it. What the approach of the dog-days is to the canine species, the approach of the honeymoon is to the human race.

sp.speaker: SERVANT.
sp.p: Lady Franklin's compliments—she will see you in the boudoir, Sir.

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: In the boudoir!—go, go—I'll come directly.
My heart beats—it must be for grief. Poor Maria!

Not a white one—just like my luck: I call on a lady to talk of the dear departed, and I've nothing about me but a cursed gaudy, flaunting, red, yellow, and blue abomination from India, which it's even indecent for a disconsolate widower to exhibit. Ah! Fortune never ceases to torment the susceptible. The boudoir!—ha! ha! the boudoir!

div.head: SCENE V.
div.stage: A Boudoir in the same house.

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN.
sp.p: Now, if my scheme does but succeed! I can't help laughing to think of it! Mum—here he comes.

sp.speaker: GRAVES
sp.p: Ah, Lady Franklin!

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN
sp.p: Ah, Mr. Graves!
Pray excuse me for having kept you so long. Is it not a charming day?

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: An east wind, ma'am! but nothing comes amiss to you!—it's a happy disposition! Poor Maria!—she too was naturally gay.

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN
sp.p: Yes, she was gay. So much life, and a great deal of spirit.

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: Spirit? Yes!—nothing could master it. She would have her own way! Ah! there was nobody like her!

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN.
sp.p: And then, when her spirit was up, she looked so handsome! Her eyes grew so brilliant!

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: Did not they?—Ah! ah! ha! ha! ha! And do you remember her pretty trick of stamping her foot?—the tiniest little foot—I think I see her now. Ah! this conversation is very soothing.

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN.
sp.p: How well she acted in your private theatricals!

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: You remember her Mrs. Oakley in “The Jealous Wife?” Ha! ha! how good it was!—ha! ha!

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN.
sp.p: Ha! ha! Yes, in the very first scene, when she came out with
“Your unkindness and barbarity will be the death of me!”

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: No—no! that's not it! more energy.
“Your unkindness and barbarity will be the DEATH of me.” Ha! ha! I ought to know how she said it, for she used to practise it on me twice a-day. Ah! poor dear lamb!

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN.
sp.p: And then she sang so well! was such a composer! What was that little French air she was so fond of?

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: Ha! ha! sprightly! was it not? Let me see—let me see.

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN
sp.p: Tum ti—ti tum—ti—ti—ti. No, that's not it.

sp.speaker: GRAVES
sp.p: Tum ti—ti—tum ti—ti—tum—tum—tum.

sp.speaker: BOTH.
sp.p: Tum ti—ti—tum ti—ti—tum—tum—tum. Ha! ha!

sp.speaker: GRAVES
sp.p: Ah! what recollections it revives! It is too affecting.

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN
sp.p: Now, if I could but get him to dance with me, we should end with being partners for life. It is affecting, but we are all mortal.
And at your Christmas party, at Cyprus Lodge, do you remember her dancing the Scotch reel with Captain Macnaughten.

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: Ha! ha! ha! To be sure—to be sure.

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN.
sp.p: Can you think of the step?—somehow thus, was it not?

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: No—no—quite wrong!—just stand there. Now then
—La—la-la-la—La, la, &c.
That's it—excellent—admirable!

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN
sp.p: Now it's coming.

div.stage: Enter Sir John, Blount, Georgina,—they stand amazed.

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: Bewitching—irresistible! It's Maria herself that I see before me! Thus—thus—let me clasp—Oh, the devil! Just like my luck!—

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: Upon my word, Mr. Graves!

sp.speaker: GEORGINA, BLOUNT.
sp.p: Encore—encore! Bravo—bravo!

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: It's all a mistake! I—I—Sir John. Lady Franklin, you see—that is to say—I.—Sainted Maria! you are spared, at least, this affliction!

sp.speaker: GEORGINA.
sp.p: Pray go on!

sp.speaker: BLOUNT.
sp.p: Don't let us interwupt you.

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: Interrupt me! I must say that this rudeness—this gross impropriety—to pry into the sorrows of a poor bereaved sufferer, seeking comfort from a sympathizing friend—But such is human nature!

sp.speaker: GEORGINA.
sp.p: But, Mr. Graves!—

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: Heartless!

sp.speaker: BLOUNT.
sp.p: My dear Mr. Graves!—

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: Frivolous!

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: Stay and dine!—

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: Unfeeling!

sp.speaker: OMNES.
sp.p: Ha!—ha!—ha!

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: Monsters! Good day to you.

div.head: SCENE VI.
div.stage: The interior of ---'s Club; night; lights, &c. Small sofa-tables, with books, papers, tea, coffee, &c. Several members grouped by the fireplace; one member with his legs over the back of his chair; another with his legs over his table; a third with his legs on the chimney-piece. To the left, and in front of the Stage, an old member reading the newspaper, seated by a small round table; to the right a card-table, before which Captain Dudley Smooth is seated, and sipping lemonade; at the bottom of the Stage another card-table.

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE.
sp.p: You don't come often to the club, Stout?

sp.speaker: STOUT.
sp.p: No; time is money. An hour spent at a club is unproductive capital.

sp.speaker: OLD MEMBER
sp.p: Waiter!—the snuff-box.

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE.
sp.p: So, Evelyn has taken to play? I see Deadly Smooth, “hushed in grim repose, awaits his evening prey.” Deep work to-night, I suspect, for Smooth is drinking lemonade—keeps his head clear—monstrous clever dog!

div.stage: Enter Evelyn; salutes and shakes hands with different members in passing up the Stage.

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: How d'ye do, Glossmore? How are you, Stout?— you don't play, I think! Political Economy never plays at cards, eh?—never has time for anything more frivolous than Rents and Profits, Wages and Labour, High Prices and Low—Corn-laws, Poor-laws, Tithes, Currency —Dot-and-go-one—Rates, Puzzles, Taxes, Riddles, and Botheration! Smooth is the man. Aha! Smooth. Piquet, eh? You owe me my revenge!

div.stage: [Members touch each other significantly; Stout walks away with the snuff-box; Old Member looks at him savagely.

sp.speaker: SMOOTH.
sp.p: My dear Alfred, anything to oblige.

sp.speaker: OLD MEMBER.
sp.p: Waiter!—the snuff-box.

div.stage: [Waiter takes it from Stout, and brings it back to Old Member.

sp.speaker: BLOUNT.
sp.p: So, so! Evelyn at it again,—eh, Glossmore?

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE.
sp.p: Yes, Smooth sticks to him like a leech. Clever fellow, that Smooth!

sp.speaker: BLOUNT.
sp.p: Will you make up a wubber?

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE.
sp.p: Have you got two others?

sp.speaker: BLOUNT.
sp.p: Yes; Flat and Green.

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE.
sp.p: Bad players.

sp.speaker: BLOUNT.
sp.p: I make it a wule to play with bad players; it is five per cent, in one's favour. I hate gambling. But a quiet wubber, if one is the best player out of four, can't do one any harm.

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE.
sp.p: Clever fellow, that Blount!

div.stage: [Blount takes up the snuff-box, and walks off with it; Old Member looks at him savagely.
[Blount, Glossmore, Flat, and Green make up a table at the bottom of the Stage.

sp.speaker: SMOOTH.
sp.p: A thousand pardons, my dear Alfred,—ninety repique —ten cards!—game!

sp.speaker: EVELYN
sp.p: Game! Before we go on, one question. This is Thursday—how much do you calculate to win of me before Tuesday next?

sp.speaker: SMOOTH.
sp.p: Ce cher Alfred! He is so droll!

sp.speaker: EVELYN
sp.p: Forty games a-night—four nights, minus Sunday— our usual stakes—that would be right, I think!

sp.speaker: SMOOTH
sp.p: Quite—if I win all—which is next to impossible.

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: It shall be possible to win twice as much, on one condition. Can you keep a secret?

sp.speaker: SMOOTH.
sp.p: My dear Alfred, I have kept myself! I never inherited a farthing—I never spent less than 4000l. a-year —and I never told a soul how I managed it.

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Hark ye, then—a word with you—

sp.speaker: OLD MEMBER.
sp.p: Waiter!—the snuff-box.

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: You understand?

sp.speaker: SMOOTH.
sp.p: Perfectly; anything to oblige.

sp.speaker: EVELYN
sp.p: It is for you to deal.

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN
sp.p: There's my precious son-in-law, that is to be, spending my consequence, and making a fool of himself.

div.stage: (Takes up the snuff-box; Old Member looks at him savagely.

sp.speaker: BLOUNT.
sp.p: I'm out. Flat, a poney on the odd twick. That's wight.—
Well, Sir John, you don't play?

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: Play? no! Confound him—lost again!

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Hang the cards!—double the stakes!

sp.speaker: SMOOTH.
sp.p: Just as you please—done!

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: Done, indeed!

sp.speaker: OLD MEMBER.
sp.p: Waiter!—the snuff-box.

sp.speaker: BLOUNT.
sp.p: I've won eight points and the bets—I never lose—I never play in the Deadly Smooth set!

div.stage: [Takes up the snuff-box; Old Member as before.

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN
sp.stage: (looking over Smooth's hand, and fidgeting backwards and forwards).
sp.p: Lord have mercy on us! Smooth has seven for his point! What's the stakes?

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Don't disturb us—I only throw out four. Stakes, Sir John?—immense! Was ever such luck?—not a card for my point. Do stand back, Sir John—I'm getting irritable!

sp.speaker: OLD MEMBER.
sp.p: Waiter!—the snuff-box.

sp.speaker: BLOUNT.
sp.p: One hundred pounds on the next game, Evelyn?

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: Nonsense—nonsense—don't disturb him! All the fishes come to the bait! Sharks and minnows all nibbling away at my son-in-law!

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: One hundred pounds, Blount? Ah! the finest gentleman is never too fine a gentleman to pick up a guinea. Done! Treble the stakes, Smooth!

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: I'm on the rack!
Be cool, Evelyn! take care, my dear boy!—now don't ye— now don't!

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: What—what? You have four queens!—five to the king. Confound the cards!—a fresh pack.
sp.stage: (Throws the cards behind him over Sir John.)

sp.speaker: OLD MEMBER.
sp.p: Waiter!—the snuff-box.

sp.speaker: FIRST MEMBER.
sp.p: I never before saw Evelyn out of temper. He must be losing immensely!

sp.speaker: SECOND MEMBER.
sp.p: Yes, this is interesting!

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: Interesting! there's a wretch!

sp.speaker: FIRST MEMBER.
sp.p: Poor fellow! he'll be ruined in a month!

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: I'm in a cold sweat.

sp.speaker: SECOND MEMBER.
sp.p: Smooth is the very devil.

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: The devil's a joke to him!

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE
sp.p: A clever fellow, that Smooth, Sir John, eh?
sp.stage: (Takes up the snuff-box; Old Member as before).
sp.p: 100l. on this game, Evelyn?

sp.speaker: EVELYN
sp.p: You! well done, the Constitution! yes, 100l.!

sp.speaker: OLD MEMBER.
sp.p: Waiter!—the snuff-box.

sp.speaker: STOUT.
sp.p: I think I'll venture!—200l. on this game, Evelyn?

sp.speaker: EVELYN
sp.p: Ha! ha! ha!—Enlightenment and the Constitution on the same side of the question at last! O, Stout, Stout!—great happiness of the greatest number— greatest number, number one! Done, Stout!—200l.!— ha! ha! ha!—I deal, Stout. Well done, Political Economy—Ha! ha! ha!

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: Quite hysterical—drivelling! Arn't you ashamed of yourselves? His own cousins!—all in a conspiracy —a perfect gang of them.

sp.speaker: STOUT
sp.p: Hush! he's to marry Sir John's daughter.

sp.speaker: FIRST MEMBER.
sp.p: What, Stingy Jack's? oh!

sp.speaker: CHORUS OF MEMBERS.
sp.p: Oh! oh!

sp.speaker: OLD MEMBER.
sp.p: Waiter!—the snuff-box.

sp.speaker: EVELYN
sp.p: No more, no more—I've done!—quite enough. Glossmore, Stout, Blount,—I'll pay you to-morrow. I—I—. Death!—this is ruinous!

div.stage: [Seizes the snuff-box; Old Member as before.

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: Ruinous? I dare say it is! What has he lost? what has he lost, Smooth? Not much? eh? eh?

sp.speaker: SMOOTH.
sp.p: Oh, a trifle, dear John!—excuse me! We never tell our winnings.—
How d'ye do, Fred?—
By the by, Charles, don't you want to sell your house in Grosvenor-square?—12,000l., eh?

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE.
sp.p: Yes, and the furniture at a valuation. About 3000l. more.

sp.speaker: SMOOTH
sp.p: Um!—Well, we'll talk of it.

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: 12 and 3—15,000l. What a cold-blooded rascal it is!—15,000l., Smooth?

sp.speaker: SMOOTH.
sp.p: Oh, the house itself is a trifle, but the establishment —I'm considering whether I have enough to keep it up, my dear John.

sp.speaker: OLD MEMBER.
sp.p: Waiter, the snuff-box!
sp.stage: (Scraping it round, and with a wry face)
sp.p: —And it's all gone!
sp.stage: (Gives it to the Waiter to fill.)

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN
sp.p: And it's all gone!

sp.speaker: EVELYN
sp.p: Ha! ha! all gone? not a bit of it. Smooth, this club is so noisy. Sir John, you are always in the way. Come to my house! come! Champagne and a broiled bone. Nothing venture, nothing have! The luck must turn, and by Jupiter we'll make a night of it!

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: A night of it!!! For Heaven's sake, Evelyn! Evelyn!!—think what you are about!—think of Georgina's feelings!—think of your poor lost mother!— think of the babes unborn!—think of—

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: I'll think of nothing! Zounds!—you don't know what I have lost, man; it's all your fault, distracting my attention! Pshaw—pshaw! Out of the way, do! Come, Smooth. Ha! ha! a night of it, my boy—a night of it!

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN
sp.p: You must not, you shall not! Evelyn, my dear Evelyn!—he's drunk—he's mad! Will no one send for the police?

sp.speaker: MEMBERS.
sp.p: Ha! ha! ha! Poor old Stingy Jack!

sp.speaker: OLD MEMBER
sp.stage: (rising for the first time, and in a great rage).
sp.p: Waiter, the snuff-box!

div.head: SCENE I.
div.stage: The Anteroom in Evelyn's house, as in Scene I. Act II. Tabouret, Macfinch, Frantz, and other tradesmen.

sp.speaker: TABOURET
sp.p: So, I hear that Mr. Evelyn is turned gamester! There are strange reports about to-day—I don't know what to make of it! We must look sharp, Mr. Macfinch, we poor tradesmen, and make hay while the sun shines.

sp.speaker: MACFINCH.
sp.p: I wuish those geeming-houses were aw at the deevil! —it's a sheam and a sin for gentlemen to gang and ruin themselves, when we honest tradesmen could do it for them with sae muckle advantage to the arts and coummerce o' the country!

div.stage: Enter Smooth from the inner room, with a pocketbook and pencil in his hand.

sp.speaker: SMOOTH
sp.p: Hum! ha! Fine pictures!—
The new-fashioned velvet, hem! good-proportioned rooms! Yes, this house is better than Glossmore's! Oh, Mr. Tabouret, the upholsterer! you furnished these rooms! All of the best? eh!

sp.speaker: TABOURET.
sp.p: Oh! the VERY best! Mr. Evelyn is not a man to grudge expense, Sir!

sp.speaker: SMOOTH.
sp.p: He is not indeed. You've been paid, I suppose, Tabouret?

sp.speaker: TABOURET.
sp.p: No, Sir, no—I never send in my bills when a customer is rich.
Bills are like trees, and grow by standing.

sp.speaker: SMOOTH.
sp.p: Humph! Not PAID? humph!

sp.speaker: MACFINCH.
sp.p: I dinna like that hoomph, there's something vara suspeecious abun' it.

sp.speaker: TABOURET
sp.p: It's the great card-player, Captain Smooth—finest player in Europe—cleaned out the Duke of Silly Val. Uncommonly clever man!

sp.speaker: SMOOTH
sp.p: Thirty-six feet by twenty-eight—Um! I think a bow-window there would be an improvement: could it be done easily, Tabouret?

sp.speaker: MACFINCH.
sp.p: If Mr. Evelyn wuishes to pool about his house, there's no mon like my friend Mr. MacStucco.

sp.speaker: SMOOTH.
sp.p: Evelyn? I was speaking of myself. Mr. MacStucco? —humph!

sp.speaker: TABOURET.
sp.p: Yourself? Have you bought the house, sir?

sp.speaker: SMOOTH.
sp.p: Bought it?—hum!—ha!—it depends—So you've not been paid yet?—um! Nor you—nor you—nor you? Hum? ah!

sp.speaker: TABOURET.
sp.p: No, sir!—what then? No fear of Mr. Evelyn! Ha! ha!

sp.speaker: OMNES
sp.p: Ha! ha!—what then?

sp.speaker: MACFINCH.
sp.p: Ah, sir, what then? I'm a puir mon with a family; this way, Captain! You've a leetle account in the buiks; an' we'll ee'n wipe it out altogether, an you'll say what you mean by that Hoom ha!

sp.speaker: SMOOTH.
sp.p: Macfinch, my dear fellow, don't oblige me to cane you; I would not have Mr. Evelyn distressed for the world. Poor fellow! he holds very bad cards. So you've not been paid yet? Don't send in your bills on any account—Mind! Yes; I don't dislike the house with some alteration. Good day to you—Hum! ha!

div.stage: [Exit, looking about him, examining the chairs, tables, &c.

sp.speaker: TABOURET.
sp.p: Plain as a pikestaff!—staked his very house on an odd trick!

div.head: SCENE II.
div.stage: The foregoing.—Enter Sharp from the inner room, agitated and in a hurry.

sp.speaker: SHARP.
sp.p: O Lord! O Lord!—who'd have thought it? Cards are the devil's book! John!—Thomas!—Harris!—
Tom, take this letter to Sir John Vesey's. If not at home, find him—he will give you a cheque. Go to his banker's and get it cashed instantly. Quick—quick off with you!

sp.speaker: TABOURET
sp.p: What's the matter?—what's the matter? How's Mr. Evelyn?

sp.speaker: SERVANT.
sp.p: Bad—very bad! Sate up all night with Captain Smooth!

sp.speaker: SHARP
sp.p: Yes, Harris, your poor master! O dear! O dear! You will take this note to the Belgian minister, Portland-place. Passport for Ostend! Have the travelling carriage ready at a moment's notice!

sp.speaker: MACFINCH
sp.p: Passport! Harkye, my mon; is he gaun to pit the saut seas between us and the siller?

sp.speaker: SERVANT.
sp.p: Don't stop me—something wrong in the chest— change of air—late hours—and Captain Smooth!

sp.speaker: SHARP
sp.p: And if the bank should break!—if the bank is broke, and he can't draw out!—bound to Smooth!

sp.speaker: TABOURET.
sp.p: Bank!—what bank?

sp.speaker: SHARP.
sp.p: Flash's bank! Flash, brother-in-law to Captain Smooth! What have you heard?—eh?—eh?

sp.speaker: TABOURET.
sp.p: That there's an awful run on it!

sp.speaker: SHARP.
sp.p: I must be off. Go—go—you can't see Mr. Evelyn to-day!

sp.speaker: TABOURET.
sp.p: My account, Sir!

sp.speaker: MACFINCH.
sp.p: I've a muckle bairns and a sma' bill!

sp.speaker: FRANTZ.
sp.p: O Sare, de great gentlemen always tink first of de tailor!

sp.speaker: SHARP.
sp.p: Call again—call again at Christmas. The bank, the cards,—the cards, the bank! O dear! O dear!

sp.speaker: TABOURET.
sp.p: The bank!

sp.speaker: MACFINCH.
sp.p: The passport!

sp.speaker: FRANTZ.
sp.p: And all dat vill be seen of de great Evelyn coat is de back of it. Donner und hagel!—I vil arrest him—I vil put de salt on de tail of it!

sp.speaker: TABOURET
sp.p: I'll slip down to the city and see how the bank goes!

sp.speaker: MACFINCH
sp.p: I'll een gang to my coosin the la'yer. Nothing but peetience for us, Mr. Tabouret.

sp.speaker: TABOURET.
sp.p: Ay, ay,—stick by each other—share and share alike —that's my way, Sir.

sp.speaker: OMNES.
sp.p: Share and share alike.

div.head: SCENE III.

sp.speaker: SERVANT.
sp.p: My master is not very well, my lord; but I'll let him know.

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE.
sp.p: I'm very curious to learn the result of his gambling tête-à-tête.

sp.speaker: BLOUNT.
sp.p: Oh, he's so howwidly wich, he can afford even a tête-à-tête with Deadly Smooth!

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE.
sp.p: Poor old Stingy Jack: why, Georgina was your intended.

sp.speaker: BLOUNT.
sp.p: Yes; and I really liked the girl, though out of pique I pwoposed to her cousin. But what can a man do against money?
If we could start fair, you'd see whom Georgina would pwefer: but she's sacwificed by her father! She as much as told me so!

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: So, so, gentlemen, we've a little account to settle— one hundred each.

sp.speaker: BOTH.
sp.p: Don't talk of it.

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Well, I won't!—

Ha! ha! you'd hardly believe it—but I'd rather not pay you just at present; my money is locked up, and I must wait, you know, for the Groginhole rents. So! instead of owing you one hundred pounds, suppose I owe you five? You can give me a cheque for the other four. And, harkye! not a word to Glossmore.

sp.speaker: BLOUNT.
sp.p: Glossmore! the gweatest gossip in London! I shall be delighted!—
It never does harm to lend to a wich man; one gets it back somehow. By the way, Evelyn, if you want my gwey cab-horse, you may have him for two hundred pounds, and that will make seven!

sp.speaker: EVELYN
sp.p: That's the fashionable usury: your friend does not take interest—he sells you a horse.—
Blount, it's a bargain.

sp.speaker: BLOUNT
sp.p: No; I don't see what harm it can do me; that off leg must end in a spavin.

sp.speaker: EVELYN
sp.p: That hundred pounds I owe you is rather inconvenient at present; I've a large sum to make up for the Groginhole property—perhaps you would lend me four or five hundred more—just to go on with?

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE.
sp.p: Certainly! Hopkins is dead: your interest for Cipher would—

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Why, I can't promise that at this moment. But as a slight mark of friendship and gratitude, I shall be very much flattered if you'll accept a splendid grey cab-horse I bought to-day—cost two hundred pounds!

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE.
sp.p: Bought to-day!—then I'm safe. My dear fellow! you're always so princely!

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Nonsense! just write the cheque; and, harkye!— not a syllable to Blount!

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE.
sp.p: Blount? He's the town-crier!

sp.speaker: BLOUNT
sp.p: Wansom's, Pall-mall.

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Thank you. So you proposed to Miss Douglas!

sp.speaker: BLOUNT.
sp.p: Hang it! yes; I could have sworn that she fancied me; her manner, for instance, that very day you pwoposed for Miss Vesey,—otherwise Georgina—

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Has only half what Miss Douglas has.

sp.speaker: BLOUNT.
sp.p: You forget how much Stingy Jack must have saved! But I beg your pardon.

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Never mind; but not a word to Sir John, or he'll fancy I'm ruined.

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE
sp.p: Ransom's, Pall-mall. Tell me, did you win or lose last night?

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Win! lose! oh! No more of that, if you love me. I must send off at once to the banker's

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE
sp.p: Why! he's borrowed from Blount, too!

sp.speaker: BLOUNT
sp.p: That's a draft from Lord Glossmore!

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Excuse me; I must dress; I have not a moment to lose. You remember you dine with me to-day—seven o'clock. You'll meet Smooth.
It may be the last time I shall ever welcome you here! My—what am I saying?—Oh, merely a joke!—good by—good by.

div.stage: [Shaking them heartily by the hand. Exit by the inner room.

sp.speaker: BLOUNT.
sp.p: Glossmore!

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE.
sp.p: Blount!

sp.speaker: BLOUNT.
sp.p: I am afraid all's not wight!

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE.
sp.p: I incline to your opinion!

sp.speaker: BLOUNT.
sp.p: But I've sold my gwey cab-horse.

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE.
sp.p: Grey cab-horse! you! What is he really worth now?

sp.speaker: BLOUNT.
sp.p: Since he is sold, I will tell you—Not a sixpence!

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE.
sp.p: Not a sixpence! he gave it to me!

div.stage: [Evelyn at the door, giving directions to a Servant in dumb show.

sp.speaker: BLOUNT.
sp.p: That was devilish unhandsome! Do you know, I feel nervous!

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE.
sp.p: Nervous? Let us run and stop payment of our drafts.

div.stage: [Evelyn shuts the door, and Servant runs across the stage.

sp.speaker: BLOUNT.
sp.p: Hollo, John! where so fast?

sp.speaker: SERVANT
sp.p: Beg pardon, Sir Frederick, to Pall-mall—Messrs. Ransom.

sp.speaker: BLOUNT
sp.p: Glossmore, we are floored!

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE.
sp.p: Sir, the whole town shall know of it!

sp.speaker: TOKE.
sp.p: Come, come, stir yourselves! we've no time to lose. This room is to be got ready for the shawls. Mrs. Crump and the other ladies of our household are to wait here on the women before they go up to the drawing-room. Take away that desk: don't be lazy! and give me the newspaper.
sp.stage: [Toke seats himself; the Servants bustle about.
sp.p: Strange reports about my patron! and the walley is gone for the passport!

sp.speaker: FRANTZ.
sp.p: Mr. Toke, my goot Mr. Toke, I've brought you von leetel present.

sp.speaker: TOKE.
sp.p: John and Charles, vanish!
I scorns to corrupt them 'ere working classes!

sp.speaker: FRANTZ
sp.stage: (producing a pair of smallclothes, which Toke examines).
sp.p: Your master is von beggar! He vants to run avay; ve are all in de same vat-you-call-it—de same leetel nasty boat, Mr. Toke! Just let my friend Mr. Clutch up through the area, and I vill arrest him dis very day.

sp.speaker: TOKE.
sp.p: I accept the abridgments; but you've forgotten to line the pockets!

sp.speaker: FRANTZ.
sp.p: Blesh my soul, so I have!

sp.speaker: TOKE.
sp.p: The area gate shall be left undefended. Do it quietly; no claw, as the French say.

sp.speaker: FRANTZ.
sp.p: Goot Mr. Toke—to-morrow I vill line de oter pocket.

sp.speaker: TOKE.
sp.p: My patron does not give me satisfaction!

sp.speaker: FOOTMAN.
sp.p: What chandeliers are to be lighted, Mr. Toke?—it's getting late.

sp.speaker: TOKE.
sp.p: Don't disturb me—I'm rum-mynating!—yes, yes, there's no doubt of it! Charles, the area gate is open?

sp.speaker: FOOTMAN.
sp.p: And all the plate in the pantry! I'll run and—

sp.speaker: TOKE.
sp.p: Not a step! leave it open.

sp.speaker: FOOTMAN.
sp.p: But—

sp.speaker: TOKE
sp.p: It's for the sake of wentilation!

div.head: SCENE V.
div.stage: A splendid Saloon in Evelyn's house.

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: You've withdrawn your money from Flash and Brisk?

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: No.

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: No!—then—

div.stage: Enter Sir John, Lady Franklin, and Georgina.

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: You got the cheque for 500l. safely?—too happy to—

sp.speaker: EVELYN
sp.p: My best thanks!—my warmest gratitude! So kind in you! so seasonable!—that 500l.—you don't know the value of that 500l. I shall never forget your nobleness of conduct.

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: Gratitude! Nobleness!—
I can't have been taken in?

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: And in a moment of such distress!

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN
sp.p: Such distress! He picks out the ugliest words in the whole dictionary!

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: I've done with Smooth. But I'm still a little crippled, and you must do me another favour. I've only as yet paid the deposit of ten per cent. for the great Groginhole property. I am to pay the rest this week— nay, I fear, to-morrow. I've already sold out of the Funds; the money lies at the bankers', and of course I can't touch it; for if I don't pay by a certain day, I forfeit the estate and the deposit.

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: What's coming now, I wonder?

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Georgina's fortune is 10,000l. I always meant, my dear Sir John, to present you with that little sum.

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: Oh, Evelyn! your generosity is positively touching!

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: But the news of my losses has frightened my tradesmen! I have so many heavy debts at this moment that—that—that—. But I see Georgina is listening, and I'll say what I have to say to her.

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: No, no—no no. Girls don't understand business!

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: The very reason I speak to her. This is an affair, not of business, but of feeling. Stout, show Sir John my Correggio.

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN
sp.p: Devil take his Correggio! The man is born to torment me!

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: My dear Georgina, whatever you may hear said of me, I flatter myself that you feel confidence in my honour.

sp.speaker: GEORGINA.
sp.p: Can you doubt it?

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: I confess that I am embarrassed at this moment; I have been weak enough to lose money at play, and there are other demands on me. I promise you never to gamble again as long as I live. My affairs can be retrieved, but for the first few years of our marriage it may be necessary to retrench.

sp.speaker: GEORGINA.
sp.p: Retrench!

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: To live perhaps altogether in the country.

sp.speaker: GEORGINA.
sp.p: Altogether in the country!

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: To confine ourselves to a modest competence.

sp.speaker: GEORGINA.
sp.p: Modest competence! I knew something horrid was coming!

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: And now, Georgina, you may have it in your power at this moment to save me from much anxiety and humiliation. My money is locked up—my debts of honour must be settled—you are of age—your 10,000l. in your own hands—

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN
sp.stage: (Stout listening as well as Sir John).
sp.p: I'm standing on hot iron!

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: If you could lend it to me for a few weeks—You hesitate! oh! believe the honour of the man you will call your husband before all the calumnies of the fools whom we call the world! Can you give me this proof of your confidence? Remember, without confidence, what is wedlock?

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN
sp.p: No!—
sp.stage: (Aloud, pointing his glass at the Correggio)
sp.p: Yes, the picture may be fine.

sp.speaker: STOUT.
sp.p: But you don't like the subject?

sp.speaker: GEORGINA
sp.p: He may be only trying me! Best leave it to papa.

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Well—

sp.speaker: GEORGINA.
sp.p: You—you shall hear from me to-morrow.—
Ah, there's that dear Sir Frederick!

div.stage: Enter Glossmore and Smooth; Evelyn salutes them, paying Smooth servile respect.

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN
sp.p: Ha! ha! To be so disturbed yesterday,—was it not droll?

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: Never recur to that humiliating topic!

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE
sp.p: See how Evelyn fawns upon Smooth!

sp.speaker: STOUT.
sp.p: How mean in him! Smooth—a professional gambler —a fellow who lives by his wits! I would not know such a man on any account!

sp.speaker: SMOOTH
sp.p: So Hopkins is dead—you want Cipher to come in for Groginhole, eh?

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE.
sp.p: What!—could you manage it?

sp.speaker: SMOOTH.
sp.p: Ce cher Charles!—anything to oblige!

sp.speaker: STOUT.
sp.p: Groginhole! What can he have to do with Groginhole? Glossmore, present me to Smooth.

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE.
sp.p: What! the gambler—the fellow who lives by his wits?

sp.speaker: STOUT.
sp.p: Why, his wits seem to be an uncommonly productive capital! I'll introduce myself. How d'ye do, Captain Smooth? We have met at the club, I think,—I am charmed to make your acquaintance in private. I say, Sir, what do you think of the affairs of the nation? Bad! very bad!—no enlightenment!—great fall off in the revenue!—no knowledge of finance! There's only one man who can save the country—and that's Popkins!

sp.speaker: SMOOTH.
sp.p: Is he in parliament, Mr. Stout? What's your Christian name, by the by?

sp.speaker: STOUT.
sp.p: Benjamin.—No; constituencies are so ignorant, they don't understand his value. He's no orator: in fact, he stammers so much—but devilish profound. Could not we ensure him for Groginhole?

sp.speaker: SMOOTH.
sp.p: My dear Benjamin, it's a thing to be thought on.

sp.speaker: EVELYN
sp.p: My friends—pray be seated;—I wish to consult you. This day twelvemonths I succeeded to an immense income, and as, by a happy coincidence, on the same day I secured your esteem, so now I wish to ask you if you think I could have spent that income in a way more worthy your good opinion.

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE.
sp.p: Impossible! excellent taste—beautiful house!

sp.speaker: BLOUNT.
sp.p: Vewy good horses—
especially the gwey cab!

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN.
sp.p: Splendid pictures!

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: And a magnificent cook, ma'am!

sp.speaker: SMOOTH
sp.p: It's my opinion, Alfred—and I'm a judge—that you could not have spent your money better!

sp.speaker: OMNES
sp.p: Very true!

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: What say you, Sir John? You may think me a little extravagant; but you know that in this world the only way to show oneself thoroughly respectable is to make a thoroughly respectable show.

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: Certainly—certainly!—No, you could not have done better.—
I don't know what to make of it.

sp.speaker: GEORGINA.
sp.p: Certainly.—
Don't retrench, my dear Alfred!

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE.
sp.p: Retrench! nothing so plebeian!

sp.speaker: STOUT.
sp.p: Plebeian, sir!—worse than plebeian!—it is against all the rules of public morality. Every one knows, now-a-days, that extravagance is a benefit to the population —encourages art—employs labour—and multiplies spinning-jennies.

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: You reassure me!—I own I did think that a man worthy of friends so sincere might have done something better than feast—dress—drink—play—

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE.
sp.p: Nonsense!—we like you the better for it.—
I wish I had my 600l. back, though.

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: And you are as much my friends now as when you offered me 10l. for my old nurse.

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: A thousand times more so, my dear boy!

sp.speaker: SMOOTH.
sp.p: But who's our new friend?

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Who! the very man who first announced to me the wealth which you allow I have spent so well. But what's the matter, Sharp?

sp.speaker: EVELYN
sp.p: The bank's broke!

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: Broke!—what bank?

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Flash, Brisk, and Co.

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE
sp.p: And Flash was your brother-in-law. I'm very sorry.

sp.speaker: SMOOTH
sp.p: Not at all, Charles,—I did not bank there.

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: But I warned you—you withdrew?

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Alas! no!

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: Oh!—Not much in their hands?

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Why, I told you the purchase-money for Groginhole was at my bankers'—But no, no: don't look so frightened! It was not placed with Flash—it is at Hoare's —it is, indeed. Nay, I assure you it is! A mere trifle at Flash's—upon my word, now! To-morrow, Sharp, we'll talk of this! One day more—one day, at least, for enjoyment!

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: Oh! a pretty enjoyment!

sp.speaker: BLOUNT.
sp.p: And he borrowed 700l. of me!

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE.
sp.p: And 600l. of me!

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: And 500l. of me!

sp.speaker: STOUT.
sp.p: Oh! a regular Jeremy Diddler!

sp.speaker: SMOOTH
sp.p: John, do you know, I think I would take a handsome offer for this house just as it stands—furniture, plate, pictures, books, bronzes, and statues!

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: Powers above!

sp.speaker: STOUT
sp.p: I say, you have placed your daughter in a very unsafe investment. What then?—a daughter's like any other capital—transfer the stock in hand to t'other speculation.

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN
sp.p: Ha! I'm afraid we've been very rude to Sir Frederick. A monstrous fine young man!

sp.speaker: TOKE
sp.p: Sir, I beg your pardon, but Mr. Macfinch insists on my giving you this letter instantly.

sp.speaker: EVELYN
sp.p: How! Sir John, this fellow, Macfinch, has heard of my misfortunes, and insists on being paid;—a lawyer's letter—quite insolent!

sp.speaker: TOKE.
sp.p: And, Sir, Mr. Tabouret is below, and declares he won't stir till he's paid.

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Won't stir till he's paid! What's to be done, Sir John?—Smooth, what is to be done?

sp.speaker: SMOOTH.
sp.p: If he won't stir till he's paid, make him up a bed, and I'll take him in the inventory as one of the fixtures, Alfred!

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: It is very well for you to joke, Mr. Smooth. But—

div.stage: Enter Sheriff's-Officer, giving a paper to Evelyn, and whispering.

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: What's this? Frantz, the tailor. Why, you impudent scoundrel! Faith! this is more than I bargained for—Sir John, I'm arrested.

sp.speaker: STOUT
sp.stage: (slapping Sir John on the back with glee).
sp.p: He's arrested, old gentleman! But I didn't lend him a farthing.

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: And for a mere song—150l.! Sir John, pay this fellow, will you? or bail me, or something,—while we go to dinner!

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: Pay—bail—I'll be d---d if I do!—Oh, my 500l.! my 500l.! Mr. Alfred Evelyn, I want my 500l.!

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: I'm going to do a very silly thing—I shall lose both my friend and my money;—just like my luck!—Evelyn, go to dinner—I'll settle this for you.

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN.
sp.p: I love you for that!

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: Do you? then I am the happiest—Ah! ma'am, I don't know what I am saying!

sp.speaker: EVELYN
sp.p: Don't go by these appearances! I repeat, 10,000l. will more than cover all my embarrassments. I shall hear from you to-morrow?

sp.speaker: GEORGINA.
sp.p: Yes—yes!

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: But you're not going?—You, too, Glossmore?—you, Blount?—you, Stout?—you, Smooth?

sp.speaker: SMOOTH.
sp.p: No; I'll stick by you—as long as you've a guinea to stake!

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE.
sp.p: Oh, this might have been expected from a man of such ambiguous political opinions!

sp.speaker: STOUT.
sp.p: Don't stop me, Sir. No man of common enlightenment would have squandered his substance in this way. Pictures and statues!—baugh!

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Why, you all said I could not spend my money better! Ha! ha! ha!—the absurdest mistake!—you don't fancy I'm going to prison?—Ha! ha!—Why don't you laugh, Sir John?—Ha! ha! ha!

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: Sir, this horrible levity!—Take Sir Frederick's arm, my poor injured, innocent child!—Mr. Evelyn, after this extraordinary scene, you can't be surprised that I— I—Zounds! I'm suffocating!

sp.speaker: SMOOTH.
sp.p: But, my dear John, they've no right to arrest the dinner!

sp.speaker: STOUT
sp.p: But the election at Groginhole is to-morrow. This news may not arrive before the poll closes!—
Sir, Popkins never bribes: but Popkins will bet you 1000l. that he don't come in for Groginhole.

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE.
sp.p: This is infamous, Mr. Stout! Cipher is a man who scorns every subterfuge!—
But, for the sake of the Constitution, name your price.

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: I know the services of Cipher—I know the profundity of Popkins: but it's too late—the borough's engaged!

sp.speaker: TOKE.
sp.p: Dinner is served.

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE
sp.p: Dinner!

sp.speaker: STOUT.
sp.p: Dinner!—it's a very good smell!

sp.speaker: EVELYN
sp.p: Turtle and venison too!

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: That's right—come along. But, I say, Blount— Stout—Glossmore—Sir John—one word first: will you lend me 10l. for my old nurse?

sp.speaker: SMOOTH and EVELYN.
sp.p: Ha! ha! ha!

div.head: SCENE I.

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE.
sp.p: Will his horses be sold, think you?

sp.speaker: SMOOTH,
sp.p: Very possibly, Charles!—a fine stud—hum! ha! Waiter, a glass of sherry!

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE.
sp.p: They say he must go abroad!

sp.speaker: SMOOTH.
sp.p: Well! it's the best time of year for travelling, Charles.

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE.
sp.p: We are all to be paid to-day; and that looks suspicious!

sp.speaker: SMOOTH.
sp.p: Very suspicious, Charles! Hum!—ah!

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE.
sp.p: My dear fellow, you must know the rights of the matter: I wish you'd speak out. What have you really won? Is the house itself gone?

sp.speaker: SMOOTH.
sp.p: The house itself is certainly not gone, Charles, for I saw it exactly in the same place this morning at half past ten—it has not moved an inch!

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE
sp.p: From Groginhole—an express! What's this? I'm amazed!!!

“They've actually at the eleventh hour started Mr. Evelyn; and nobody knows what his politics are! We shall be beat!—the constitution is gone!—Cipher!” Oh! this is infamous in Evelyn! Gets into parliament just to keep himself out of the Bench.

sp.speaker: SMOOTH.
sp.p: He's capable of it!

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE.
sp.p: Not a doubt of it, Sir!—not a doubt of it!

div.stage: Enter Sir John and Blount, talking.

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: My dear boy, I'm not flint! I am but a man! if Georgina really loves you—and I am sure that she does—I will never think of sacrificing her happiness to ambition—she is yours; I told her so this very morning.

sp.speaker: BLOUNT.
sp.p: The old humbug!

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: She's the best of daughters!—the most obedient artless creature! Oh! she's been properly brought up: a good daughter makes a good wife. Dine with me at seven, and we'll talk of the settlements.

sp.speaker: BLOUNT.
sp.p: Yes; I don't care for fortune; but—

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: Her 10,000l. will be settled on herself—that of course.

sp.speaker: BLOUNT.
sp.p: All of it, Sir? Weally I—

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: What then, my dear boy? I shall leave you both all I've laid by. Ah! you know I'm a close fellow! “Stingy Jack”—eh? After all, worth makes the man!

sp.speaker: SMOOTH.
sp.p: And the more a man's worth, John, the worthier man he must be!

sp.speaker: BLOUNT
sp.p: Yes; he has no other child! She must have all his savings; I don't see what harm it could do me. Still that 10,000l.—I want that 10,000l.: if she would but run off now, one could get rid of the settlements.

div.stage: Enter Stout (wiping his forehead), and takes Sir John aside.

sp.speaker: STOUT.
sp.p: Sir John, we've been played upon! My secretary is brother to Flash's head clerk; Evelyn had not 300l. in the bank!

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: Bless us and save us! you take away my breath! But then—Deadly Smooth—the arrest—the—oh, he must be done up!

sp.speaker: STOUT.
sp.p: As to Smooh, he'd “do anything to oblige.” All a trick, depend on it! Smooth has already deceived me, for before the day's over Evelyn will be member for Groginhole. I've had an express from Popkins; he's in despair! not for himself—but for the country, Sir John—what's to become of the country?

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: But what could be Evelyn's object?

sp.speaker: STOUT.
sp.p: Object? Do you look for an object in a whimsical creature like that? A man who has not even any political opinions! Object! Perhaps to break off his match with your daughter! Take care, Sir John, or the borough will be lost to your family!

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: Aha! I begin to smell a rat! But it's not too late yet.

sp.speaker: STOUT.
sp.p: My interest in Popkins made me run to Lord Spendquick, the late proprietor of Groginhole. I told him that Evelyn could not pay the rest of the money; and he told me that—

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: What?

sp.speaker: STOUT.
sp.p: Mr. Sharp had just paid it him; there's no hope for Popkins! England will rue this day!

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: Georgina shall lend him the money! I'll lend him—every man in my house shall lend him—I feel again what it is to be a father-in-law! But stop; I'll be cautious. Stout may be on his side—a trap—not likely; but I'll go first to Spendquick myself. Sir Frederick, excuse me—you can't dine with me to-day. And, on second thoughts, I see that it would be very unhandsome to desert poor Evelyn now he's down in the world. Can't think of it, my dear boy—can't think of it. Very much honoured, and happy to see you as a friend. Waiter! my carriage! Um! What, humbug Stingy Jack, will they? Ah! a good joke, indeed!

sp.speaker: BLOUNT.
sp.p: Mr. Stout, what have you been saying to Sir John? Something against my character; I know you have; don't deny it. Sir, I shall expect satisfaction!

sp.speaker: STOUT.
sp.p: Satisfaction, Sir Frederick? as if a man of enlightenment had any satisfaction in fighting! Did not mention your name; we were talking of Evelyn. Only think!—he's no more ruined than you are.

sp.speaker: BLOUNT.
sp.p: Not wuined? Aha, now I understand!—So, so! Stay, let me see—she's to meet me in the square!
sp.stage: (pulls out his watch; a very small one.)

sp.speaker: STOUT
sp.stage: (pulling out his own; a very large one).
sp.p: I must be off to the vestry.

sp.speaker: BLOUNT.
sp.p: Just in time!—ten thousand pounds! Gad, my blood's up, and I won't be tweated in this way, if he were fifty times Stingy Jack!

div.head: SCENE II.
div.stage: The drawing-rooms in Sir John Vesey's house.

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: Well, well, I am certain that poor Evelyn loves Clara still: but you can't persuade me that she cares for him.

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN.
sp.p: She has been breaking her heart ever since she heard of his distress. Nay, I am sure she would give all she has could it save him from the consequences of his own folly.

sp.speaker: GRAVES
sp.p: She would only give him his own money, if she did. I should like just to sound her.

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN
sp.p: And you shall. I take so much interest in her that I forgive your friend everything but his offer to Georgina.
Where are the young ladies?

sp.speaker: SERVANT.
sp.p: Miss Vesey is, I believe, still in the square: Miss Douglas is just come in, my lady.

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN.
sp.p: What, did not she go out with Miss Vesey?

sp.speaker: SERVANT.
sp.p: No, my lady; I attended her to Drummond's, the banker.

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN.
sp.p: Drummond's!
Why, child, what on earth could take you to Drummond's at this hour of the day?

sp.speaker: CLARA
sp.p: Oh, I—that is—I—Ah, Mr. Graves! How is Mr. Evelyn? How does he bear up against so sudden a reverse?

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: With an awful calm. I fear all is not right here!
—The report in the town is, that he must go abroad instantly—perhaps to-day!

sp.speaker: CLARA.
sp.p: Abroad!—to-day!

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: But all his creditors will be paid; and he only seems anxious to know if Miss Vesey remains true in his misfortunes.

sp.speaker: CLARA.
sp.p: Ah! he loves her so much, then!

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: Um!—That's more than I can say.

sp.speaker: CLARA.
sp.p: She told me, last night, that he said to the last that 10,000l. would free him from all his liabilities—that was the sum, was it not?

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: Yes; he persists in the same assertion. Will Miss Vesey lend it?

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN
sp.p: If she does I shall not think so well of her poor dear mother; for I am sure she'd be no child of Sir John's!

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: I should like to convince myself that my poor friend has nothing to hope from a woman's generosity.

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN.
sp.p: Civil! And are men, then, less covetous?

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: I know one man, at least, who, rejected in his poverty by one as poor as himself, no sooner came into a sudden fortune than he made his lawyer invent a codicil which the testator never dreamt of, bequeathing independence to the woman who had scorned him.

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN.
sp.p: And never told her?

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: Never! There's no such document at Doctors' Commons, depend on it! You seem incredulous, Miss Clara! Good day!

sp.speaker: CLARA
sp.p: One word, for mercy's sake! Do I understand you right? Ah, how could I be so blind! Generous Evelyn!

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: You appreciate, and Georgina will desert him. Miss Douglas, he loves you still.—If that's not just like me! Meddling with other people's affairs, as if they were worth it—hang them!

sp.speaker: CLARA.
sp.p: Georgina will desert him. Do you think so?—
Ah, he will soon discover that she never wrote that letter!

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN.
sp.p: She told me, last night, that she would never see him again. To do her justice, she's less interested than her father,—and as much attached as she can be to another. Even while engaged to Evelyn she has met Sir Frederick every day in the square.

sp.speaker: CLARA.
sp.p: And he is alone—sad—forsaken—ruined. And I, whom he enriched—I, the creature of his bounty—I, once the woman of his love—I stand idly here to content myself with tears and prayers! Oh, Lady Franklin, have pity on me—on him! We are both of kin to him—as relations we have both a right to comfort! Let us go to him—come!

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN.
sp.p: No! it would scarcely be right—remember the world—I cannot.

sp.speaker: CLARA.
sp.p: All abandon him—then I will go alone!

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN.
sp.p: You!—so proud—so sensitive!

sp.speaker: CLARA.
sp.p: Pride—when he wants a friend?

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN.
sp.p: His misfortunes are his own fault—a gambler!

sp.speaker: CLARA.
sp.p: Can you think of his faults now? I have no right to do so. All I have—all—his gift!—and I never to have dreamt it!

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN.
sp.p: But if Georgina do indeed release him—if she has already done so—what will he think? What but—

sp.speaker: CLARA.
sp.p: What but—that, if he love me still, I may have enough for both, and I am by his side! But that is too bright a dream. He told me I might call him brother! Where, now, should a sister be?—But— but—I—I—I tremble! If, after all—if—if—In one word—Am I too bold? The world—my conscience can answer that—but do you think that HE could despise me?

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN.
sp.p: No, Clara, no! Your fair soul is too transparent for even libertines to misconstrue. Something tells me that this meeting may make the happiness of both! You cannot go alone. My presence justifies all. Give me your hand—we will go together!

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Yes; as yet, all surpasses my expectations. I am sure of Smooth—I have managed even Sharp; my election will seem but an escape from a prison. Ha! ha! True, it cannot last long; but a few hours more are all I require, and for that time at least I shall hope to be thoroughly ruined.
Well, Graves, and what do people say of me?

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: Everything that's bad!

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Three days ago I was universally respected. I awake this morning to find myself singularly infamous. Yet I'm the same man.

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: Humph! why gambling—

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Cant! it was not criminal to gamble—it was criminal to lose. Tut!—will you deny that, if I had ruined Smooth instead of myself, every hand would have grasped mine yet more cordially, and every lip would have smiled congratulation on my success? Man— Man! I've not been rich and poor for nothing! The Vices and the Virtues are written in a language the World cannot construe; it reads them in a vile translation, and the translators are—Failure and Success! You alone are unchanged.

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: There's no merit in that. I am always ready to mingle my tears with any man.

I know I'm a fool, but I can't help it. Hark ye, Evelyn! I like you —I'm rich; and anything I can do to get you out of your hobble will give me an excuse to grumble for the rest of my life. There, now it's out.

sp.speaker: EVELYN
sp.p: There's something good in human nature after all! My dear friend, did I want your aid I would accept it, but I can extricate myself yet. Do you think Georgina will give me the same proof of confidence and affection?

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: Would you break your heart if she did not?

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: It is in vain to deny that I still love Clara; our last conversation renewed feelings which would task all the energies of my soul to conquer. What then? I am not one of those, the Sybarites of sentiment, who deem it impossible for humanity to conquer love—who call their own weakness the voice of a resistless destiny. Such is the poor excuse of every woman who yields her honour, of every adulterer who betrays his friend. No! the heart was given to the soul as its ally, not as its traitor.

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: What do you tend to?

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: This:—If Georgina still adheres to my fortunes (and I will not put her to too harsh a trial), if she can face the prospect, not of ruin and poverty, for reports wrong me there, but of a moderate independence; if, in one word, she love me for myself, I will shut Clara for ever from my thought. I am pledged to Georgina, and I will carry to the altar a soul resolute to deserve her affection and fulfil its vows.

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: And if she reject you?

sp.speaker: EVELYN
sp.p: If she do I am free once more! And then—then I will dare to ask, for I can ask without dishonour, if Clara can explain the past and bless the future!

sp.speaker: EVELYN
sp.p: The die is cast—the dream is over! Generous girl. Oh, Georgina! I will deserve you yet.

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: Georgina, is it possible?

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: And the delicacy, the womanhood, the exquisite grace of this! How we misjudge the depth of the human heart! How, seeing the straws on the surface, we forget that the pearls may lie hid below! I imagined her incapable of this devotion.

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: And I too!

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: It were base in me to continue this trial a moment longer: I will write at once to undeceive that generous heart

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: I would have given 1000l. if that little jade Clara had been beforehand: but just like my luck! if I want a man to marry one woman, he's sure to marry another on purpose to vex me!

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Take this instantly to Miss Vesey; say I will call in an hour.
And now Clara is resigned for ever! Why does my heart sink within me? Why, why, looking to the fate to come, do I see only the memory of what has been?

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: You are re-engaged then to Georgina!

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Irrevocably.

div.head: SCENE IV.
div.stage: Enter Servant, announcing Lady Franklin and Miss Douglas.—Evelyn, Graves.

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN.
sp.p: My dear Evelyn, you may think it strange to receive such visitors at this moment; but, indeed, it is no time for ceremony. We are your relations—it is reported you are about to leave the country—we come to ask frankly what we can do to serve you?

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Madam—I—

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN.
sp.p: Come, come—do not hesitate to confide in us; Clara is less a stranger to you than I am: your friend here will perhaps let me consult with him.—
Let us leave them to themselves.

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: You're an angel of a widow; but you come too late, as whatever is good for anything generally does.

div.stage: [They retire into the inner room, which should be partially open.

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Miss Douglas, I may well want words to thank you; this goodness—this sympathy—

sp.speaker: CLARA
sp.p: Evelyn! Evelyn! Do not talk thus!—Goodness! sympathy!—I have learned all—all! It is for ME to speak of gratitude! What! even when I had so wounded you—when you believed me mercenary and cold—when you thought that I was blind and base enough not to know you for what you are;—even at that time you thought but of my happiness—my fortunes— my fate!—And to you—you—I owe all that has raised the poor orphan from servitude and dependence! While your words were so bitter, your deeds so gentle! Oh, noble Evelyn, this, then, was your revenge!

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: You owe me no thanks; that revenge was sweet! Think you it was nothing to feel that my presence haunted you, though you knew it not?—that in things, the pettiest as the greatest, which that gold could buy —the very jewels you wore—the very robe in which, to other eyes, you might seem more fair—in all in which you took the woman's young and innocent delight—I had a part—a share? that even if separated for ever— even if another's—even in distant years—perhaps in a happy home, listening to sweet voices, that might call you “mother!”—even then should the uses of that dross bring to your lips one smile—that smile was mine—due to me—due, as a sacred debt, to the hand that you rejected—to the love that you despised!

sp.speaker: CLARA.
sp.p: Despised! See the proof that I despised you!—see: in this hour, when they say you are again as poor as before, I forget the world—my pride—perhaps too much my sex: I remember but your sorrow—I am here!

sp.speaker: EVELYN
sp.p: O, Heaven! give me strength to bear it!—
And is this the same voice that, when I knelt at your feet—when I asked but one day the hope to call you mine—spoke only of poverty, and answered, “Never?”

sp.speaker: CLARA.
sp.p: Because I had been unworthy of your love if I had ensured your misery. Evelyn, hear me! My father, like you, was poor—generous; gifted, like you, with genius—ambition; sensitive, like you, to the least breath of insult. He married, as you would have done —married one whose only dower was penury and care! Alfred, I saw that genius the curse to itself!—I saw that ambition wither to despair!—I saw the struggle— the humiliation—the proud man's agony—the bitter life—the early death!—and heard over his breathless clay my mother's groan of self-reproach! Alfred Evelyn, now speak! Was the woman you loved so nobly to repay you with such a doom?

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Clara, we should have shared it!

sp.speaker: CLARA.
sp.p: Shared? Never let the woman who really loves comfort her selfishness with such delusion! In marriages like this the wife cannot share the burden; it is he—the husband—to provide, to scheme, to work, to endure—to grind out his strong heart at the miserable wheel! The wife, alas, cannot share the struggle—she can but witness the despair! And, therefore, Alfred, I rejected you.

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Yet you believe me as poor now as I was then.

sp.speaker: CLARA.
sp.p: But I am not poor; we are not so poor! Of this fortune, which is all your own—if, as I hear, one-half would free you from your debts, why, we have the other half still left, Evelyn! It is humble—but it is not penury.

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Cease, cease—you know not how you torture me. Oh, that when hope was possible!—oh, that you had bid me take it to my breast and wait for a brighter day!

sp.speaker: CLARA.
sp.p: And so have consumed your life of life upon a hope perhaps delayed till age—shut you from a happier choice, from fairer fortunes—shackled you with vows that, as my youth and its poor attributes decayed, would only have irritated and galled—made your whole existence one long suspence! No, Alfred, even yet you do not know me!

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Know you! Fair angel, too excellent for man's harder nature to understand!—at least it is permitted me to revere. Why were such blessed words not vouchsafed to me before?—why, why come they now—too late? Oh, Heaven—too late!

sp.speaker: CLARA.
sp.p: Too late! What, then, have I said?

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Wealth! what is it without you? With you, I recognise its power; to forestall your every wish—to smooth your every path—to make all that life borrows from Grace and Beauty your ministrant and handmaid; and then, looking to those eyes, to read there the treasures of a heart that excelled all that kings could lavish;—why that were to make gold indeed a god! But vain—vain—vain! Bound by every tie of faith, gratitude, loyalty, and honour, to another!

sp.speaker: CLARA.
sp.p: Another! Is she, then, true to your reverses? I did not know this—indeed, I did not! And I have thus betrayed myself! O, shame! he must despise me now!

div.head: SCENE V.
div.stage: The foregoing.—Enter Sir John; at the same time Graves and Lady Franklin advance from the inner room.

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN
sp.p: Evelyn, I was hasty yesterday. You must own it natural that I should be so. But Georgina has been so urgent in your defence, that—
sp.stage: (as Lady Franklin comes up to listen)
sp.p: Sister, just shut the door, will you? —that I cannot resist her. What's money without happiness? So give me your security; for she insists on lending you the 10,000l.

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: I know; and have already received it.

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: Already received it! Is he joking? Faith, for the last two days I believe I have been living amongst the Mysteries of Udolpho! Sister, have you seen Georgina?

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN.
sp.p: Not since she went out to walk in the square.

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN
sp.p: She's not in the square nor the house—where the deuce can the girl be?

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: I have written to Miss Vesey—I have asked her to fix the day for our wedding.

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN
sp.p: Have you? Go, Lady Franklin, find her instantly —she must be back by this time: take my carriage, it is but a step—you won't be two minutes gone.—
I'd go myself, but I'm afraid of leaving him a moment while he's in such excellent dispositions.

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN
sp.p: No, no: stay till I return.

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: And don't be downhearted, my dear fellow; if the worst come to the worst, you will have everything I can leave you. Meantime, if I can in any way help you—

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Ha!—you!—you, too? Sir John, you have seen my letter to Miss Vesey?
or could she have learned the truth before she ventured to be generous?

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: No; on my honour. I only just called at the door on my way from Lord Spend—that is, from the City. Georgina was out;—was ever anything so unlucky?—
[Hurrah—hurrah! Blue for ever!]—What's that?

sp.speaker: SHARP.
sp.p: Sir, a Deputation from Groginhole—poll closed in the first hour—you are returned! Hollow, Sir— hollow!

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: And it was to please Clara!

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: Mr. Sharp,—Mr. Sharp,—I say, how much has Mr. Evelyn lost by Messrs. Flash and Co.

sp.speaker: SHARP.
sp.p: Oh, a great deal, Sir,—a great deal.

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN
sp.p: How!—a great deal!

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Speak the truth, Sharp,—concealment is all over.

sp.speaker: SHARP.
sp.p: 223l. 6s. 3d.—a great sum to throw away.

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: Ah, I comprehend now! Poor Evelyn, caught in his own trap!

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: Eh! what, my dear boy?—what? Ha! ha! all humbug, was it?—all humbug, upon my soul! So, Mr. Sharp, isn't he ruined after all?—not the least, wee, rascally, little bit in the world, ruined?

sp.speaker: SHARP.
sp.p: Sir, he has never even lived up to his income.

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: Worthy man! I could jump up to the ceiling! I am the happiest father-in-law in the three kingdoms.— And that's my sister's knock too.

sp.speaker: CLARA.
sp.p: Since I was mistaken, cousin,—since, now, you do not need me,—forget what has passed; my business here is over. Farewell!

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Could you but see my heart at this moment, with what love, what veneration, what anguish it is filled, you would know how little, in the great calamities of life, fortune is really worth. And must we part now, —now, when—when—I never wept before, since my mother died!

div.stage: Enter Lady Franklin and Georgina, followed by Blount, who looks shy and embarrassed.

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: Georgina herself—then there's no hope.

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: What the deuce brings that fellow Blount here?— Georgy, my dear Georgy, I want to—

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Stand back, Sir John.

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: But I must speak a word to her—I want to—

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Stand back, I say,—not a whisper—not a sign. If your daughter is to be my wife, to her heart only will I look for a reply to mine.

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN
sp.p: Speak the truth, niece.

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Georgina, it is true, then, that you trust me with your confidence—your fortune. Is it also true that, when you did so, you believed me ruined? O, pardon the doubt! Answer as if your father stood not there—answer me from that truth the world cannot yet have plucked from your soul—answer as if the woe or weal of a life trembled in the balance—answer as the woman's heart, yet virgin and unpolluted, should answer to one who has trusted to it his all!

sp.speaker: GEORGINA.
sp.p: What can he mean?

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN
sp.p: She won't look this way, she won't!—hang her! —Hem!

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: You falter. I implore—I adjure you—answer!

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN.
sp.p: The truth!

sp.speaker: GEORGINA.
sp.p: Mr. Evelyn; your fortune might well dazzle me, as it dazzled others. Believe me, I sincerely pity your reverses.

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: Good girl: you hear her, Evelyn?

sp.speaker: GEORGINA.
sp.p: What's money without happiness?

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: Clever creature!—noble sentiment!

sp.speaker: GEORGINA.
sp.p: And, so, as our engagement is now annulled,—papa told me so this very morning,—I have promised my hand where I have given my heart—to Sir Frederick Blount.

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: I told you,—I? No such thing—no such thing: you frighten her out of her wits—she don't know what she's saying.

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Am I awake? But this letter—this letter, received to-day—

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN
sp.p: Drummond's!—from a banker!

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Read—read.

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN.
sp.p: “Ten thousand pounds just placed to your account— from the same unknown friend to Alfred Evelyn.” Oh, Clara, I know now why you went to Drummond's this morning!

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Clara! What!—and the former one with the same signature—on the faith of which I pledged my hand and sacrificed my heart—

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN.
sp.p: Was written under my eyes, and the secret kept that—

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: Look up, look up, Clara—I am free!—I am released! you forgive me?—you love me?—you are mine! We are rich—rich! I can give you fortune, power,—I can devote to you my whole life, thought, heart, soul—I am all yours, Clara—my own—my wife!

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: A pretty mess you've made of it, to humbug your own father! And you, too, Lady Franklin—I am to thank you for this!

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN.
sp.p: You've to thank me that she's not now on the road to Scotland with Sir Frederick; I chanced on them by the Park just in time to dissuade and save her. But, to do her justice, a hint of your displeasure was sufficient.

sp.speaker: GEORGINA
sp.p: And you know, papa, you said this very morning that poor Frederick had been very ill used, and you would settle it all at the club.

sp.speaker: BLOUNT.
sp.p: Come, Sir John, you can only blame yourself and Evelyn's cunning device! After all I'm no such vewy bad match; and as for the 10,000l.—

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: I'll double it. Ah, Sir John, what's money without happiness?

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: Pshaw—nonsense—stuff! Don't humbug me.

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN.
sp.p: But if you don't consent, she'll have no husband at all.

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: Hum! there's something in that.—
Double it, will you? Then settle it all tightly on her. Well—well—my foible is not avarice. Blount, make her happy. Child, I forgive you.—
Ugh, you fool!

sp.speaker: GRAVES
sp.p: I'm afraid it's catching. What say you? I feel the symptoms of matrimony creeping all over me. Shall we? eh? Shall we? Frankly, now, frankly—

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN.
sp.p: Frankly, now, there's my hand, on one condition,— that we finish our reel on the wedding-day.

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: Accepted. Is it possible? Sainted Maria! thank Heaven you are spared this affliction.

sp.speaker: SMOOTH.
sp.p: How d'ye do, Alfred?—I intrude, I fear! Quite a family party.

sp.speaker: BLOUNT.
sp.p: Wish us joy, Smooth—Georgina's mine, and—

sp.speaker: SMOOTH.
sp.p: And our four friends there, apparently have made up another rubber. John, my dear boy, you look as if you had something at stake on the odd trick.

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: Sir, you're very—Confound the fellow!—and he's a dead shot too!

div.stage: Enter Stout and Glossmore hastily, talking with each other.

sp.speaker: STOUT.
sp.p: I'm sure he's of our side; we've all the intelligence.

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE.
sp.p: I'm sure he's of ours if his fortune is safe, for we've all the property.

sp.speaker: STOUT.
sp.p: Just heard of your return, Evelyn! Congratulate you. The great motion of the session is fixed for Friday. We count on your vote. Progress with the times!

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE.
sp.p: Preserve the Constitution!

sp.speaker: STOUT.
sp.p: Your money will do wonders for the party!— Advance!

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE.
sp.p: The party respects men of your property! Stick fast!

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: I have the greatest respect, I assure you, for the worthy and intelligent flies upon both sides the wheel; but whether we go too fast or too slow does not, I fancy, depend so much on the flies as on the Stout Gentleman who sits inside and pays the post-boys. Now all my politics as yet is to consider what's best for the Stout Gentleman!

sp.speaker: SMOOTH.
sp.p: Meaning John Bull. Ce cher old John!

sp.speaker: STOUT.
sp.p: I'm as wise as I was before.

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE.
sp.p: Sir, he's a trimmer!

sp.speaker: EVELYN
sp.p: Ah, Clara, you—you have succeeded where wealth had failed! You have reconciled me to the world and to mankind. My friends—we must confess it—amidst the humours and the follies, the vanities, deceits, and vices that play their part in the Great Comedy of Life—it is our own fault if we do not find such natures, though rare and few, as redeem the rest, brightening the shadows that are flung from the form and body of the TIME with glimpses of the everlasting holiness of truth and love.

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: But for the truth and the love, when found, to make us tolerably happy, we should not be without—

sp.speaker: LADY FRANKLIN.
sp.p: Good health;

sp.speaker: GRAVES.
sp.p: Good spirits;

sp.speaker: CLARA.
sp.p: A good heart;

sp.speaker: SMOOTH.
sp.p: An innocent rubber;

sp.speaker: BLOUNT.
sp.p: A pwoper degwee of pwudence;

sp.speaker: STOUT.
sp.p: Enlightened opinions;

sp.speaker: GLOSSMORE.
sp.p: Constitutional principles;

sp.speaker: SIR JOHN.
sp.p: Knowledge of the world;

sp.speaker: EVELYN.
sp.p: And—plenty of Money!
